Commentary.Commentary: Around 28 overs left in the day. How much can South Africa score tonight? How many wickets can the Kiwis get? The visitors will be aiming to get a lead of around 50 by the end of play while the home side will look for a wicket or two before the deficit is erased. Stay tuned for the third innings.

A disciplined bowling performance from the Proteas. Wickets were hard to come by, so they stuck to bowling tight lines, not giving anything away. Philander and Morkel picked up 2 apiece while Rabada got 1. Maharaj profited the most, with a 5-wicket haul.

A similar batting performance from New Zealand as that of the Proteas. Kane Williamson scored a patient 130 to match Dean Elgar's 140 while Raval and Watling scored half centuries similar to the ones made by du Plessis and Bavuma. Philander played a crucial knock for the Saffas while Wagner's cameo took the Kiwis into the lead. A like-for-like performance.

A lead of 33 may sound paltry but in the context of the game, it could be defining. Wagner's counter-attacking run-a-ball 32 has given the Kiwis something to smile and with the pitch starting to wear, it could be more than a handful.

Excellent bowling by South Africa. They have toiled and toiled and eventually reaped rewards. They are just two wickets away from batting again, which might be just 1, given that Ross Taylor may not bat. Everyone has bowled well, barring JP Duminy who was just looking to fill in the overs anyway.

It was the last hour which brought a change in fortune for the Proteas -  the use of the second new ball. Williamson was dismissed by Rabada and then Santner and Watling got dismissed quickly. They played out a lot of balls, but could not manage to add the same volume of runs.
A riveting session of cricket. Just 57 runs scored in 26 overs with 3 wickets lost. South Africa have kept the pressure on and it has resulted in pegging the Kiwis back.

... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...
It has gone a little overcast in the last few minutes. Hopefully, there is no rain. Join us back at 1340 local (0040 GMT) for the second session.

South Africa bowled okay, getting a little bit of reverse swing. They had a terrific first hour but were ordinary in the second. They will look to have a good hour post lunch and bundle out New Zealand quickly.

Williamson has played like the iron man. He started slowly today, not scoring for a long time but then has played at a very decent strike rate. He has received good support from Watling and the Kiwis will hope for more resistance from the rest of the batsmen.

70/2 in 27 overs inn that session. Pretty much even-stevens. South Africa will be happy with the fact that they did not the Kiwis run away with the game while the hosts will be happy about eating into the deficit. It is 61 now and they will be confident that they can get into the lead after the break.

OUT! Caught behind! Controversial decision. There does not seem to be any part of the foot behind the popping crease. However, the third umpire feels it is a legal delivery. Neesham is not too happy. Leaving that side, it was a terrific piece of bowling. Morkel lands it on a good length outside off, could have been left alone but Neesham feels for it. He gets a thin outside edge and de Kock does the rest. Umpire Dharmasena straightaway raises his finger but then wants to cross-check the overstepping. It seems very close. From the angles shown, when the front foot lands, the back heel seems to be in front of the crease, not behind. Morkel seems to have got away with one. NEW ZEALAND STILL TRAIL BY 115.
Neesham has been caught behind! But is it a no ball? The umpires are checking...
Full and wide outside off, Jimmy flays hard but misses.
A bouncer down the leg side, Neesham ducks.
Full and down the leg side, Williamson misses his flick. Yet to score a run this morning.
Ooohh..... on a good length around middle, Jimmy looks to flick but the ball goes off the inside edge through fine leg. A run taken.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On a good length outside off, let through again.
Closer to the stumps outside off, left alone.
WIDE! Oh dear... that probably slipped out of Rabada's hands. He bowled this way outside off, even outside the pitch, Neesham let it go and the ball almost went to Hashim Amla at first slip.
On a good length outside off, Williamson thinks to play at that but then decides to bail out. The ball comes back in a long way.
Angles this down the leg side, Neesham clips it towards fine leg for a single.
Full and outside off, angling in, JN defends watchfully.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
A bouncer outside off, Jimmy sways away.
On a good length outside off, Neesham looks to defend but then decides to take his bat away. Is late and the ball goes off the bottom edge towards the slip cordon.
MORNE MORKEL comes on to bowl now.
Full and wide outside off, KW lets it go.
Full and down the leg side, Kane misses his flick.
Fuller and wider outside off, easily left alone.
A bouncer but down the leg side, Williamson ducks.
Landed outside off, coming in, dabbed towards gully.
On a good length outside off, defended watchfully.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
On a good length around off, Neesham looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto the pads and the ball rolls back to the bowler.
A bit too straight, worked straight to square leg.
Outside off, played towards point.
A terrific yorker on middle and leg, tailing in, Jimmy somehow manages to work it through square leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone once more.

LBW appeal! Turned down! A short ball around middle, Neesham looks to pull but gets hit on the pads. Rabada appeals, so does the slip cordon, but the umpire is unmoved. Faf does not take the review. Replays show the ball taking the inside edge on its way.
On a good length closer to the off stump, angling away, shouldered arms to again.
Full and wide outside off, pretty wide, left alone.
Slants it on the pads, Neesham works it through square leg for a couple. The deficit is now 119.
Back of a length outside off, pushed towards cover again.
Similar ball, moving away, this time Kane goes back and punches it towards cover.
On a good length outside off, Williamson comes forward and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a good length outside off, Neesham plays inside the line and is beaten.
Gets across to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards square leg and the batsmen take a leg bye.
One more leave outside off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a couple.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

OUT! That is a sensational catch! Faf du Plessis has pulled off a stinger. It was a length ball outside off and Patel looked to slash it over the top. He got a thick outside edge which flew over second slip but du Plessis threw himself to his right, went at it one-handed, but then could not hang on. However, he grabbed it in the second attempt, again one-handed. Philander gets his second scalp.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Another good shot. Full outside off, JP drives it through cover-point. Dean Elgar gets to it, puts in a slide near the ropes and saves the boundary. Temba Bavuma tidies up and the batsmen take three.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a good length around off, defended watchfully.
Good comeback from the bowler. Lands it in the corridor of uncertainty, on a good length just outside off, Jeetan feels for it but gets beaten.

FOUR! BRILLIANT! This is a lovely shot. Half volley outside off, Patel reaches out and just pushes the ball away. It is in the gap, past short extra cover and the outfield takes the ball to the fence. The deficit is now 127. Patel moves into double figures.
Full and outside off, coming in, Patel offers a solid defensive shot towards cover off the front foot.
KAGISO RABADA to share the attack from the other end.
Outside off, blocked towards gully.
Finally makes the batsman play, lands it on a good length just outside off, Kane defends watchfully.
Four in a row. Wide outside off, shouldered arms to.
Similar ball, once again no shot offered.
On a good length this time, wider than the previous one, left alone again.
Full and outside off, a touch wide and Williamson is happy to let it go.
The players are out in the middle. South Africa's first task will be to remove the night watchman JEETAN PATEL as quickly as possible. Here is VERNON PHILANDER. He will bowl to KANE WILLIAMSON. Play!
PITCH REPORT - The footmarks are slowly getting darker on the surface. There might be more instances of turn today but the track is still a good one to bat. Batsmen need to be patient.
WEATHER - Yet another stunning day in Dunedin. Not a cloud in the sky. Should be great conditions to play cricket.

Day 3 is often considered as the pivotal day of a Test match. Today is no different. New Zealand trail by 131 and have 7 wickets left, which might be 6 because of Ross Taylor's absence. South Africa will feel they are a wicket away from enforcing a collapse while the Kiwis will bank on their dependable middle and lower middle order. Williamson remains the key. Who will come out on top? Hello and a warm welcome to the third day's play of the opening Test between New Zealand and South Africa in Dunedin.

To be honest, South Africa did not bowl that well today. They were too full or too wide and will aim to rectify that tomorrow. Do join us at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous night) to see who takes control on the most important Day 3 of the Test. Until then, you can catch all the action from the ongoing SL-Ban Test match and a little later, the third ODI between West Indies and England. Adios! Take Care!

Kane Williamson was the key today and will be the key tomorrow as well. He started off slowly but then got into rhythm with a flurry of boundaries. He is batting on 78 but needs support from the middle and lower middle order.

Keshav Maharaj was the man responsible for the dismissals of Raval and Nicholls. He bowled beautifully from one end, getting drift and turn and that is why it is important for each side that the lead be big or small. Batting last would be difficult on this track. New Zealand would want to bat once and bat big. But now, they might be a batsman short if Taylor's injury is serious. South Africa will be aiming to bowl out the Kiwis in the morning session tomorrow and perhaps get a lead of around 50.

Decent session for both sides. The Proteas managed to pick up two wickets, almost three, with Ross Taylor retiring hurt. The home side, on the other hand, made 118 runs in 31 overs. The match hangs nicely in the balance.

A round-arm delivery to end the over, almost like a left-arm Malinga type, full and outside off, Patel leans and pushes it towards cover amidst huge cheers from the crowd. STUMPS ON DAY 2, NEW ZEALAND TRAIL BY 131!
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
Down the leg side, Jeetan misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads past the keeper. The batsmen think about the single but then Williamson sends Patel back.
Full on leg stump, flicked towards the leg side.
Last over of the day then...
Full delivery outside off, Williamson plays an exquisite drive, directly to the mid off fielder though!
Fuller and around off, swings away, Williamson goes forward and dead-bats it.
Bowls this a lot straighter and on the sticks, Williamson knocks it back to the bowler.
Bowls this outside off, Williamson offers a front foot defense.
Full delivery and on the sticks, Williamson just brings his bat down and drives it down the ground.
Length ball around off, Williamson pushes it towards covers.
FOUR! Full delivery and outside off, Patel is channeling his inner No 5 batsman, creams it through covers to get back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Loose delivery from Maharaj, bowls the low full toss again. Think he wants the magic delivery to spin it back from the leg stump. Flicked away to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Patel defends this looped up delivery towards the leg side.
Fuller delivery around off, Patel blocks it towards silly point. Cries of catch it come from the slip cordon, but the catch wasn't there.
Drags his length back and bowls it around off, Patel goes on his back foot to stonewall.
Tossed up and around leg, tucked away through mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Fullish delivery, angling away, Patel taps it towards point.
Full delivery, this time it comes back in, Patel leans and blocks it towards the cover region.
Good length delivery pitched on off, but it goes away and whizzes past Patel's bat as he looks to defend it. Beauty of a delivery.
On a length and on the sticks, Patel knocks it down the ground.
Williamson guides this length ball to third man for an easy single.

Chance? No, falls short! Fuller delivery, swings away, Williamson wants to block but only manages a genuine edge which goes towards the keeper, who dives ahead and to his right to catch it. However, KW had played it with soft hands and the ball fell well ahead of Quinton de Kock.
Bowls it slower through the air and on the sticks, Patel defends it.
Floats this one outside off, Patel comes forward and stonewalls.
Patel has blocked this looped up delivery towards the leg side.
Sprays this down the leg side, clipped away through backward square leg. One run taken.
Bowls this one around leg, Patel lunges to block but it takes the leading edge and goes towards point. Enough for Williamson to regain the strike. Single taken.
The nightwatchman Jeetan Patel arrives at the crease.

OUT! The catch is legal! The bowling change works. Oh and Amla grabs a stunner. Full delivery around off, HN goes forward to defend but it takes the outside edge and goes towards first slip, where Hashim dives to his left and takes a sharp and low one-handed catch. Oh hold on for a second, replays indicate that the ball might have touched the ground. And the umpires have taken it upstairs. The soft  signal is out. And multiple replays gives the third umpire no conclusive evidence to overturn the decision. He thinks it is a clean catch and Nicholls has to depart.
Maharaj strikes first ball on return! Amla has taken a beauty. But the third umpire wants to check whether it is legal.
Time for spin. Keshav Maharaj is back on.
We are done with the scheduled close of play but because 5 overs are remaining, it has been extended. South Africa have 30 minutes to complete their quota of overs for the day.
Marginally ahead of length, around off and middle, Williamson goes on his back foot and blocks it.
Philander is consistently reversing the ball now. Full again and swings away, KW lunges forward and offers a front foot defense.
Full ball which swings away so Williamson has offered no shot.
Bowls this full outside off, KW lets it through to the keeper.
Fuller delivery again, KW defends it with an angled bat towards square leg.
Fullish delivery, which swings away, KW stands firm in his crease and buries it onto the ground.
Lands this on a length, fourth stump line, left alone.
Length ball, around off, Nicholls pushes it towards the off side.
Fuller delivery, manages to get a good shape there, but it is outside off and HN shoulders his arms.
Short of a length outside off, HN gets out of its way.
Length ball outside off, HN ignores it.
Back of a length delivery, sharply comes back in, Williamson nudges it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total!
Fuller delivery and on the pads, Nicholls flicks it straight to the mid-wicket fielder.
Length ball, outside off, HN has decided to offer no shot.
Philander goes round the wicket and bowls a length ball outside off, HN lunges forward and defends it towards the off side.
Back of a length delivery, outside off, driven through point for a single.
Fullish delivery, comes back in, KW dead-bats it from his crease.
Pitches this on a length outside off, KW punches it on the up to the cover fielder.
Shortish delivery, outside off, HN leaves it alone.
Good length delivery outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms.
Length ball around off, Nicholls wants to steer it down to third man but it takes the inside edge and goes onto hit his pads.
On a length around off, HN defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Terrific shot. Short and wide, Nicholls leaps a bit and cuts it through point for a boundary. There was no fielder there and he got what he wanted.
Length ball around middle and leg, Williamson flicks it away towards the leg side for a single.
The batsman gets an inside edge on that which goes fine down the leg side.
Nicholls goes on the front foot and defends this length ball.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Fuller delivery and on the sticks, Nicholls drives it elegantly through mid off for a boundary.
Length ball around off, HN offers front foot defense.

NOT OUT! But it was total miscommunication, oh captain what did you do there? On a length around leg, Nicholls tucks it through square leg and sets off. The call was only for two, but Kane thinks there was a third. How wrong was he? He was miles down the pitch, but the fielder in the deep threw it towards the keeper which gave Williamson some extra time to recover. De Kock throws it towards Philander who disturbs the bails at the non striker's end. South Africa appeal and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays show that KW has made his ground with a full stretched dive. Close shave that!
The umpires have gone upstairs for a run out. Williamson is in danger and he has no one but himself to blame.
Vernon Philander is reintroduced into the attack! He will bowl from around the wicket to Henry Nicholls!
Good length delivery, on the sticks, Williamson blocks it off his back foot.
Marginally ahead of length, sixth stump line, Williamson watches it carefully and offers no shot.
Bouncer! Outside leg, Williamson ducks and it was out of his reach.

The word from the New Zealand camp is that Ross Taylor has a calf injury. Certainly did not look good when he was limping off the field, with the help of the physio. Only time will tell whether he can take part in the remainder of the match and series.
On a length outside off, Williamson leaves it alone.
Back of a length delivery, outside off, KW pushes it towards the point region.
Length ball, Morkel manages to extract extra bounce, Williamson taps it towards point. Bavuma runs across from deep backward point to stop the ball. Two runs added to the total!
Sprays this towards leg, Nicholls flicks it on the up albeit straight to the mid-wicket fielder.
Fullish delivery, around off, lunges forward and is solid in defense.
Fuller and angling in, flicked off the pads to square leg. Runs two to get off the mark and brings up  the 150-run mark for his side.
On a length outside off, HN shoulders his arms.
Fuller delivery around off, Nicholls defends it towards point.
Length delivery, way outside off, Nicholls sees it go to the keeper.
Henry Nicholls strolls out to replace Ross Taylor.

The physio is out in the middle. However, it is not for the hit Taylor got on the helmet but for something in his right hamstring or calf. Some stretching is going on. Bad news for the hosts, Taylor is walking off. Not a good sign at all for New Zealand. Wonder whether he is out of the match or it just a precaution.
The short ball again, Williamson gets away with it but in the process loses his balance and almost falls on the ground.
On a length, which nips back in, clipped to fine leg for an easy single.
Length ball, around leg, Taylor flicks it away through fine leg. Two runs added to the total! Morkel has been wayward so far in his new spell.
FOUR LEG BYES! Bangs this short, Taylor looks to get away from the ball but it hits his helmet which parries it over the keeper. De Kock gives it a chase only to come second.
Length and around middle and leg, Taylor looks to tuck it away but misses and the ball raps his thigh pad.
Sprays this down the leg side, Taylor offers no shot. The keeper drives to his left and gathers the ball.
Ends the over with a yorker, Taylor jams it out towards the leg side and runs one.
Length and slightly outside, but that is what Taylor needs for a cut. He plays that shot but straight towards covers.
Full and around off, Taylor defends it from the crease.
Steams in and hits the deck hard, Taylor allows de Kock to do his work.
On a length, outside off, pats it towards point and steals a quick a single. Duminy hurls a throw at the striker's end but it was well away. It would've been close had it been a direct hit.
Fuller delivery, swings in sharply, Taylor flicks it with an angled bat through mid-wicket. One run added to the total!
Closer to the off stump, short in length, left alone again.
Landed outside off, left alone.
A short ball around middle and off, Kane looks to hook but misses.
FOUR! BRILLIANT! Half volley outside off, Williamson leans and drives it through the covers for yet another boundary! T%he stand moves to 21.

Full and just around off, Williamson drives it straight back and it hits the stumps at the other end. Morne Morkel appeals for a run out but the umpire does not even bother going upstairs. Replays show why. Morne did not even touch the ball.
Full and around off, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
MORNE MORKEL is back on.
Fuller and on the sticks, Kane defends it.
Back of a length delivery, KW goes on his back foot and drills it through covers. The fielder at covers runs behind it and stops the ball. Two runs added to the total!
Williamson drives this length ball towards the leg side.
FOUR! Williamson is scoring just in boundaries all of a sudden! On a length and outside off, Williamson gets on his toes and drives it through covers for a boundary!
Length ball and outside off, punched to covers.
Bangs this short, Williamson leaves it alone after ducking under it.
Drinks have been taken.
Fuller and on the sticks, Taylor leans forward and offers a front foot defense.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Taylor goes forward and blocks this tossed up delivery.
Bowls a low full toss, Taylor flicks it to mid-wicket.
Short and on off, Taylor makes room and drives it very late through point and cover-point. The fielders chase it to save a boundary and they do! Two runs added to the total!
Full delivery and on the sticks, Taylor uses his feet and knocks it to the mid off fielder.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson stands deep in his crease and dead-bats it.
Length delivery and comes back in, Williamson clips it through square leg. Two runs added to the total!
Shortish delivery, nips back in, KW hops to defend and almost drags it back  on the stumps. But it bounces and goes over the sticks.
Bowls this on a length and on the pads, Williamson blocks it towards the leg side.
Ripper! Lands this on a length, fifth stump line, KW looks to defend but it whistles past the outside edge.
Full and around off, Williamson defends it towards the slip cordon.
Full and on middle, eased down towards mid on. One run added to the total!
Shorter and on leg, Williamson goes back to tuck it away but it hits his pad. South Africa appeal but it is turned down!
Williamson clips this tossed up delivery towards backward square leg.
Fuller delivery and around off, Williamson goes forward to block.
Drags his length back and around off, Williamson goes on his back foot and blocks.
FOUR! Bowls a full toss around leg, Williamson duly punishes it. Just flicks it to the vacant deep mid-wicket region for a boundary!
Leg bye! Angles in a length delivery, around leg, KW looks to tuck it away but it goes off his pad towards fine leg. They run a leg bye!
Bangs this one short again, the ball stays low but Williamson has ducked very well and ball goes past him to the keeper.
Shorter delivery and coming back in, Williamson ducks and QDK gathers it.
Back of a length around off, KW goes on the back foot and defends it.
On a length, which nips back in sharply, Williamson knows where his off stump is and leaves it alone.
Length delivery and around off, KW hops and dead-bats it.
Tosses this one on middle, flicked away to mid-wicket.
Pitched on middle, Taylor goes forward and defends it off his outside edge towards covers.
Sprays this down the leg side, Taylor strides forward and defends it.
ROSS TAYLOR walks in at number 4, replacing Raval.

OUT! A wicket out of nowhere and to a ball which actually didn't deserve it. Short and around leg, Raval looks to play it through square but the ball stops on him and he hands a straight catch to Elgar at mid-wicket. Maharaj breaks the partnership! Raval would be disappointed to throw his wicket away like this!
Looped up delivery outside off, Raval leans and blocks it.
Tosses this one outside off, Raval goes forward to stonewall.
Length and outside off, Williamson leaves it alone.
26th Test Fifty for Williamson. It has been an excellent knock and he has blossomed as the innings has progressed. That brings up the 100-run stand as well.
FOUR! On a length and outside off, Williamson just places it through Bavuma, who was deployed at point, and it goes for a boundary. Three consecutive boundaries for the skipper!
FOUR! Bowls another full delivery slightly around leg, Williamson plays a similar shot and the mid on fielder again has no other option but to bring the back on from the long on fence.
FOUR! Classy shot! Fuller and on the sticks, Williamson just offers full face of the bat and ball rushes past mid on for a boundary.
On a length outside off, punched towards the off side.
Starts the over with a bouncer, Williamson ducks and leaves it alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Raval goes forward and buries this looped up delivery onto the ground.
Tossed up around off, Raval has blocked.
Bowls this on the pads, clips it away to mid-wicket.
Jeet Raval brings up his 3rd Test fifty!
FOUR! What a way to bring up his milestone. Fuller and outside off, Raval drives it past the mid off fielder for a boundary!
Tosses this one outside off, Raval looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge past the first slip. They run two.
Short of a length delivery, around off, Williamson defends it on the back foot towards covers.
Back of a length delivery around middle and leg, Williamson gets on his toes and forces it towards mid-wicket.
Angles this on a length and around leg, Raval clips it through fine leg. One run added to the total!
Sprays this down the leg side, Raval tucks it away through backward square leg to take a couple.
Lands this on a length and brings it back in, Raval blocks it offering a full face of the bat.
Back of a length delivery, around off, Raval stands deep in his crease and buries it onto the ground.
Kagiso Rabada is back on, he will replace Vernon Philander.
Slower through the air and on off, Williamson looks to steer it towards third man but it takes the outside edge and goes towards Amla at first slip. However, the ball falls short of him.
FOUR! Loops this one slightly outside off, enough for Williamson to make room and cut it through point for a boundary. Beautiful placement!
Tossed up, outside off, lunges forward and dead-bats it.
Angles this on the pads, Williamson defends it towards the FSL.
KW knocks this tossed up delivery back to the bowler.
Sprays this down the leg side, Williamson looks to sweep but misses and it hits his front pad.
Fuller delivery and nipping back in, Williamson's flick goes through the mid-wicket fielder who gives it a chase to cut it off. Three runs added to the total!
On a length and comes back in, KW knocks it towards mid off.
Length and around pads, flicked away through mid-wicket for a single.

NO BALL! FOUR! He will have to bowl that ball again! Short of a length and around leg, the southpaw stands tall and pulls it with complete authority through square leg for a boundary. That was a Steve Finn-esque no ball, he disturbed the bails at the non striker's end when he was in his run-up.
Philander switches to over the wicket now...

FOUR! Drives this one perfectly! Full and swinging away, Raval reaches out to the ball and creams it between the point and cover-point fielder for a boundary. The fielders give it a chase only to come second.
Fullish delivery, nips back in, Raval looks to drive but it goes off the inside edge towards square leg.
Lands this on a length and way outside off, Raval has a look at it and allows QDK to collect it.
Loops this one on the fourth stump line, Williamson pushes it towards the bowler.
Drags his length back and outside off, Williamson is rock solid in defense.

Half volley and on leg, Williamson drives it down the ground towards mid on, where Rabada dives to make a save but instead parries it towards long off. Elgar gives it a chase and cuts it off. Two runs taken!
Williamson nudges this shortish delivery towards the leg side.
Fullish and on the pads, KW uses his feet and clips it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up on the sticks, KW goes on the back foot and blocks it with the full face of the bat.
Short of a length delivery, around the pads, Raval shuffles across a touch and pushes it back to the bowler.
Philander, goes around the wicket, pitches this on a length and outside off, let through to the keeper.
On a length and on the pads, Raval looks to flick but it takes the outside edge and rolls towards covers.
Back of a length delivery, around off, Raval gets on his toes and blocks it.
Length ball outside off, Raval watchfully leaves it alone.

FOUR! Full and angling into the pads, Raval moves across and clips it effortlessly through mid-wicket for a boundary. Lovely shot that. That region was vacant and the southpaw gets the expected result.
FOUR! On middle and leg, Williamson flicks it away and gets a boundary!
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

EDGED, SAFE! Landed outside off, late drift, Raval lunges to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge past Hashim Amla at first slip towards third man. Three runs taken. Raval moves to 30. The deficit is now 239.
Full and outside off, Raval comes down the track and drives it towards mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Lands this on a length on the pads, Williamson flicks towards mid-wicket.
Marginally ahead of length angling in, Williamson nudges it towards the leg side.
Angles in a back of a length ball, which comes back in, Raval pulls it through mid-wicket. One run taken.
Full delivery around off, Raval looks to drive but it goes off the inner half of the bat to the bowler.
Bowls this one outside off on a length, left alone.
Length ball, nips back in, Raval defends it from the crease.
VERNON PHILANDER to bowl from the other end.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, swept through square leg for a couple.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Williamson rocks back and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Welcome back for the final session. 31 overs left. If the Kiwis do not lose more than a wicket, this could be their day. Here is Keshav Maharaj to kane Williamson.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

South Africa have not done badly but there is nothing in the pitch to assist them. They will have to rely on probing lines and lengths and some mistakes from the batsmen for wickets. Join us back at 1600 local (0300 GMT) for the final session.

Good comeback from New Zealand. Lost Latham early but a steady stand between Williamson and Raval has kept the Proteas at bay. Philander threatened to break their concentration, but Raval and Williamson have been excellent.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket. TEA ON DAY 2, NEW ZEALAND TRAIL BY 249!
Comes forward and flicks it away for a single. The deficit is now 249.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, blocked watchfully.
FOUR! Short on middle, Williamson goes back and pulls it through square leg for a boundary. Moves to 20 with his second boundary. The stand is worth 43 now.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
JP DUMINY to bowl the final over before Tea.
Full and outside off, well blocked out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle and leg, flicked to the leg side.
Full and outside off, Raval comes forward watchfully and defends.
Shorter on middle, worked through mid-wicket. Temba Bavuma gives it a chase and the batsmen take three.
Full and down the leg side, flicked straight to square leg.
Comes around the wicket, bowls it on middle, defended watchfully.
Down the leg side, tucked fine. The ball races across the turf but Kagiso Rabada gives it a good chase from deep backward square leg. Dives full length and prevents the boundary. Two runs taken.
Terrific delivery. Lands it on a good length around off, Raval looks to defend but the ball seams back in a long way and cuts Raval into two, just missing the off stump.

Fabulous shot. Fractionally short of a length outside off, Williamson gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers. Temba Bavuma gives it a chase from cover and the batsmen take three. The deficit is now 259.
Landed outside off, pushed towards cover.
A short ball down the leg side, pulled down to fine leg for a single.

Ooohh.... Williamson comes down the track and has a big swing. He is not to the pitch of the ball and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. It goes behind, just past de Kock and lands short of Hashim Amla at first slip.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Full on middle and leg, Williamson comes down the track and pushes it towards mid on for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on middle and leg, flicked towards short leg.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
Down the leg side, Jeet misses his tuck and is hit op the pads. Morkel appeals for LBW but the umpire turns it down. Nothing in it.
On a good length around middle, defended watchfully.
Looks to work it away but misses and is hit on the pads. A leg bye taken.
Perfect line and length, in the corridor of uncertainty, Williamson lets it through.
On a good length just around off, defended watchfully.
Quicker around off, Raval goes back and blocks it towards cover.
Full and around middle and off, defended towards point.
Comes around the wicket now. Amla is standing extremely fine at first slip.
Fuller and outside off, pushed with a lunge towards cover.
On a good length outside off, punched towards mid off but Maharaj gets across to stop.
Very full outside off, dabbed across to the off side.
Looped up on middle, defended back to the bowler.

Good length again, outside off, angled in, dabbed straight to gully.
Closer than the previous one, on a good length, left alone.
Shorter and wider outside off, slapped straight to point.

FOUR! That is a shot right out of the textbook. Short ball outside off, Williamson gets on the back foot and punches it through the covers with both feet off the ground at the point of impact. That is not an easy shot to play. The deficit is now 266.
On a good length outside off, nice testing stuff from Morkel, Williamson gets on top of the bounce and defends.
Full again, driven straight to cover.
FOUR! Too much width from Maharaj, fuller in length, Maharaj opens the face of the bat and drives it behind point for the second boundary of the over! Moves to 22 and the stand is worth 23.
Thrown up a bit outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Full and outside off, watchfully patted to the off side.

FOUR! This time he gets it. Repeat does of the previous ball, full and outside off, this time Raval is upto it. Reaches out, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through cover-point for a boundary.
Drifted away from the left-hander, wide outside off, fuller in length, Raval looks to drive but misses.
On a good length around off, Kane lets it go. The ball comes in a long way and then deviates away. Lovely bowling.
A bouncer on middle, Williamson ducks.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
On a good length around off, worked towards mid on.

Full and outside off, Williamson pushes it towards cover. He understands that it is Dean Elgar who is at cover-point and he is a left-hander. So he has to get to the ball and then turn to throw with his left hand. A single us taken in the meanwhile. Excellent judgement.
Drifting in on the pads, KW sweeps it towards square leg.
A touch shorter, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller this time, Kane leans and pushes it towards point.
Starts off with a short ball outside off, Williamson goes back and punches it towards cover.
Double change. KESHAV MAHARAJ to bowl his left-arm orthodox.
Keeps this one full and straight, JR defends.
Fuller this time, another left alone outside off.
Wider outside off, shouldered arms to again.
Another one outside off, Raval patiently watches it go past.
Wider outside off, let through again.
Full and outside off, left alone.
MORNE MORKEL comes in as the first change.
Landed outside off, tapped towards cover.
Around off, pushed towards cover for a quick single. The deficit is now 279.
On a good length around off, defended watchfully.
Full and just outside off, shouldered arms to.
Tests him with a bouncer, Jeet ducks.
On a good length around off, Raval defends towards cover.
Very well bowled, straight and full, KW blocks.

A bit loose. Full and outside off, Raval attempts a cover drive but his bottom hand comes off the bat. The ball goes off the toe end wide of point. Temba Bavuma gives it a good chase and just stops it near the ropes. Three runs taken.
Full and just outside off, defended towards cover.
Full and straight, coming in from around the wicket, pushed towards mid on.
Just drifting onto the leg stump, slightly full, Kane works it wide of mid on. By the time Morne Morkel can get to it. three runs are taken. The stand moves to double figures.
Good leave. On a fuller length outside off, Williamson initially thinks of playing at it but then takes his bat away at the last moment.
Outside off, another leave.
On a good length outside off, good pace and bounce, Raval lets it go.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Full again, outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Full and just around off, defended watchfully.
A full toss outside off, driven straight to cover.
That is a beauty. On a good length outside off, Williamson commits into a forward defense but the ball curves away and beats the outside edge.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, let through.
The batsman gets a bottom edge of the bat on that one.
Around middle and off, watchfully blocked out.
NO BALL! Philander oversteps by a large margin and bowls it on middle and leg, worked behind square leg for a single.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Landed outside off, dabbed towards gully.
Outside off, Williamson leans and drives it through the covers but Stephen Cook dives to his left to make a brilliant stop.
Landed slightly wider outside off, Williamson makes another leave.
On a good length in the avenue of apprehension, Williamson makes a good leave.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Gets off the mark. Philander strays on the pads and Williamson clips it towards deep backward square leg for a single.

Excellent bowled. On a good length around off, seaming away, well played too. Williamson trusts the bounce and movement and lets it go.
Goes right back in his crease and blocks.

Another close call. Raval taps this to the off side and sets off slowly. Temba Bavuma comes charging in, is airborne and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Raval would have been gone. Almost similar to the way he ran out Warner in Australia a few months ago.
Outside off, left alone.
Full on middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a single.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Landed around off, defended watchfully.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a couple.
Right on the money, as you would expect, around a good length on off, Williamson defends.
KANE WILLIAMSON walks in at number 3, replacing Latham.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Philander has struck. He was bowling impeccable lines till now and eventually gets a wicket. He lands this on a fuller length, but well outside off and makes the ball deviate a touch. Latham could have left it alone but he feels for it and gets a healthy nick. Simple catch for his counterpart de Kock. Philander could well like this pitch. He seems to have identified something on the pitch. NEW ZEALAND TRAIL BY 293.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards backward square leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Right on the money, around good length on middle and off, pushed to the leg side.
Beauty. On a good length around off, angling away, Raval pushes at it but misses.
Full on middle and leg, Latham looks to flick but gets a leading edge wide of Rabada towards mid off.
CHANCE! JR taps it with soft hands towards cover and sets off for a quick single. Rabada quickly gets to the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. LATHAM WAS A GONER.
A wild bouncer way outside off, Jeet ducks.
Full and just outside off, pushed towards cover.
On a good length around middle, defended from the crease.
A bouncer down the leg side, Raval ducks.

Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full again, pushed towards point once more.

Outside off, pushed towards point again.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point.
Full and around off, worked through square leg for a single. Moves to 10.
Full and just outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Landed outside off, left alone.

FOUR! EDGED AWAY! Rabada finds his mark, lands it on an in-between length of full and good, Latham pushes at it but the ball goes off the outside edge, albeit all along the ground, between second slip and gully to the third man fence. The deficit is now 296.
Better delivery, on a length outside off, angled in, shouldered arms to.
Switches to around the wicket very early on, comes in from wide of the crease and bowls it outside off. Left alone.
Full and straight again, another watchful block.
Full and straight, watchfully blocked this time.
A half-leave. Full and outside off, JR comes forward to defend, then decides to take his bat away. Is late and the ball goes of the bottom edge, on the bounce to second slip.
Full and outside off, Jeet lets it go again and this time the ball swings back in a long way but after it is past the stumps.
Similar delivery, shouldered arms to again.
On a good length outside off, Raval shoulders arms.
VERNON PHILANDER to bowl from the other end.
On a good length angling away from the left-hander, left alone.

FOUR! BEAUTY! Rabada is searching for that swing, not getting any. Bowls it nice and full outside off, a bit wide, with a slightly scrambled seam, Latham leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary.
Nicely played. Full and outside off, Raval pushes this down the ground past mid off. The fielder gets to the ball and the batsmen take three.

That is a quick single. Fill ad around off, Tom taps it towards cover and sets off for a single. Temba Bavuma comes charging in from point,. picks up the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Raval was in though.
